title: Phenotypic Characterization of the Working Heart
author: E. Dale Abel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8a2hsge

steps.title: Prepare and Isolate Mouse Heart
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse for heart isolation and remove the organ.

substeps.instruction: Heparinize mice (as early as 4 weeks old) via intraperitoneal injection of 200μl heparin (1000USP units/ml).
Induce deep anesthesia by injecting chloral hydrate at a dose of 0.7mg/g body weight.
Remove the heart from the mouse.
Dissect and trim the heart of fat and extraneous pulmonary tissue.

steps.title: Cannulate and Perfuse Heart
steps.instruction: Cannulate the heart and establish the perfusion flow.

substeps.instruction: Cannulate the aorta first using an 18G steel cannula.
Initially perfuse the heart in retrograde mode with Krebs Henseleit Buffer (KHB).
Cannulate the pulmonary vein.
Reverse perfusate flow so buffer enters the left side of the heart via the pulmonary vein and is ejected via the aorta.

steps.title: Prepare Working Heart Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the KHB working heart buffer with specific concentrations based on the experimental model.

substeps.instruction: Prepare KHB containing (in mM): 118.5 NaCl, 25 NaHCO3, 4.7 KCl, 1.2 MgSO4, 1.2 KH2PO4, 2.5 CaCl2, 0.5 EDTA.
Gas the buffer with 95% O2 - 5% CO2.

Supplement with palmitate bound to 3% BSA and glucose at concentrations determined by the model: either 0.4 mM palmitate and 5 mM glucose (normal systemic concentrations) or 1.2 mM palmitate and 11 mM glucose (e.g., for db/db mice).
Add 1nM insulin if measuring insulin responsiveness; otherwise, omit.

steps.title: Perform Perfusion and Sample Collection
steps.instruction: Perfuse the heart and collect samples for metabolic analysis over a 60-minute period.

substeps.instruction: Perfuse hearts at a preload of 15 mmHg.
Obtain pressure and flow measurements every 10 minutes throughout the 60-minute perfusion.
Withdraw a 2.5-ml sample of buffer every 20 minutes (starting at 0 min) for metabolite determination, performing all determinations in duplicate.

steps.title: Process Heart Tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest and process the heart for dry mass calculation.

substeps.instruction: Quickly freeze hearts between metal blocks cooled to -80°C at the end of the experiment.
Rapidly weigh the hearts and store at -80°C.
Pulverize hearts under liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle.
Weigh a sample of heart tissue (~20 mg) for wet weight (WHW), then dry to constant weight for dry weight.
Calculate the dry-to-wet weight ratio to determine total dry mass of the heart.

steps.title: Measure Substrate Metabolism
steps.instruction: Measure glycolysis, glucose oxidation, and palmitate oxidation using separate sets of hearts.

substeps.instruction: Measure glycolytic flux by quantifying 3H2O released from [5-3H] glucose (specific activity = 400 Mbq/mol).
Measure glucose oxidation by trapping and measuring 14CO2 released from [U-14C] glucose (specific activity = 400 Mbq/mol).

Measure palmitate oxidation in a separate set of hearts by quantifying 3H2O released from [9,10-3H] palmitate (specific activity = 18.5 Gbq/mol), accounting for endogenous fatty acid content of the BSA.

steps.title: Determine Myocardial Oxygen Consumption
steps.instruction: Measure oxygen consumption (MVO2) at 20-minute intervals in hearts used for palmitate oxidation.

substeps.instruction: Collect pulmonary artery effluent (PvO2) using a capillary tube.
Determine the oxygen content of freshly oxygenated buffer (PaO2).
Measure oxygen concentrations using a fiber-optic oxygen sensor (Ocean Optics Inc) coated with ruthinium red (emits fluorescence at 600 nm).

Calculate MVO2 (ml/min/g WHW) using the formula: ((PaO2 - PvO2)/100) x (Coronary flow/WHW) x (725/760) x (1000 x C), where C = 0.0212, 725 and 760 are atmospheric pressures (mmHg), and WHW is wet heart weight (g).
Calculate Cardiac hydraulic work [J/min/g WHW] = CO (ml/Min) x DevP (mm Hg) x 1.33 x 10-4 /g WHW.
Calculate Cardiac efficiency (%) = Hydraulic work / MVO2 x 100.
Convert MVO2 (ml/min) to μmol/min by multiplying by 0.0393, then to Joules (J/min) using 1μmol O2 = 0.4478 J.
